name: Data Structures and Algorithms
description: The core structures and algorithms every program is built from — complexity analysis, lists, stacks and queues, sorting, hashing, trees, heaps and graph traversal.

topics.name: Algorithmic Complexity
topics.summary: Describing how cost grows with input size, so two algorithms can be compared without running them.

subtopics.name: Asymptotic Notation
subtopics.summary: Big-O, Omega and Theta, and what they do and do not tell you.

objectives.text: State the formal definition of big-O and apply it to a given function
Rank common growth rates from slowest to fastest growing
Explain why constant factors are omitted and when that matters in practice

subtopics.name: Analysing Loops and Recursion
subtopics.summary: Counting operations in nested loops and solving simple recurrences.

objectives.text: Derive the time complexity of nested loops from their bounds
Write and solve the recurrence for a divide-and-conquer algorithm
Analyse the space complexity of a recursive algorithm

subtopics.name: Best, Average and Worst Case
subtopics.summary: Which case matters, and why amortised cost is different again.

objectives.text: Distinguish best-, average- and worst-case complexity for a given algorithm
Explain amortised analysis using dynamic array growth
Choose which case to optimise for given a stated requirement

topics.name: Linear Structures
topics.summary: Sequences with different cost trade-offs — the first real design decision in a program.

subtopics.name: Arrays and Dynamic Arrays
subtopics.summary: Contiguous storage, random access, and doubling growth.

objectives.text: State the cost of access, append, insert and delete for a dynamic array
Explain why doubling on growth gives amortised O(1) append
Choose an array over a linked list with justification

subtopics.name: Linked Lists
subtopics.summary: Singly and doubly linked nodes, insertion and deletion, and the cost of traversal.

objectives.text: Implement insertion and deletion at a known node in a linked list
Compare singly and doubly linked lists for a given access pattern
Explain why indexing a linked list is O(n)

subtopics.name: Stacks and Queues
subtopics.summary: LIFO and FIFO discipline, and the problems each solves naturally.

objectives.text: Implement a stack and a queue with O(1) operations
Use a stack to evaluate an expression or check balanced brackets
Explain how a circular buffer implements a queue over an array

topics.name: Sorting
topics.summary: The most studied problem in computing, and a showcase of algorithm design techniques.

subtopics.name: Elementary Sorting Algorithms
subtopics.summary: Insertion, selection and bubble sort — quadratic, but not useless.

objectives.text: Trace insertion sort and selection sort on a small array
State the time and space complexity of each elementary sort
Explain why insertion sort is preferred for small or nearly-sorted inputs

subtopics.name: Merge Sort
subtopics.summary: Divide, conquer and merge — a stable O(n log n) sort with extra space.

objectives.text: Describe the divide-and-conquer structure of merge sort
Derive the O(n log n) running time from its recurrence
Explain what stability means and why merge sort is stable

subtopics.name: Quicksort and Lower Bounds
subtopics.summary: Partitioning, pivot choice, the quadratic worst case, and why comparison sorting cannot beat n log n.

objectives.text: Trace the partition step of quicksort for a given pivot
Explain when quicksort degrades to O(n²) and how pivot choice mitigates it
State the comparison-sorting lower bound and the idea behind its proof

topics.name: Searching and Hashing
topics.summary: Finding an item fast — by ordering it, or by computing where it should be.

subtopics.name: Binary Search
subtopics.summary: Halving a sorted range, and the invariant that makes it correct.

objectives.text: Implement binary search with correct loop bounds
State the loop invariant that guarantees correctness
Explain why the input must be sorted and the cost of sorting first

subtopics.name: Hash Tables
subtopics.summary: Hash functions, buckets, load factor and expected constant-time lookup.

objectives.text: Explain how a hash function maps a key to a bucket index
State the average and worst-case cost of hash table lookup
Describe what makes a good hash function

subtopics.name: Collision Resolution
subtopics.summary: Chaining and open addressing, load factor and rehashing.

objectives.text: Compare separate chaining with open addressing
Explain how load factor affects performance and when to rehash
Trace insertion into a hash table with linear probing

topics.name: Trees
topics.summary: Hierarchical structure with logarithmic depth — the workhorse of ordered data.

subtopics.name: Binary Trees and Traversal
subtopics.summary: Structure, height, and in-order, pre-order, post-order and level-order traversal.

objectives.text: Perform in-order, pre-order, post-order and level-order traversals
Relate the height of a binary tree to its number of nodes
Implement a traversal both recursively and with an explicit stack or queue

subtopics.name: Binary Search Trees
subtopics.summary: The ordering invariant, search, insertion, deletion, and degeneration to a list.

objectives.text: State the BST invariant and use it to search for a key
Insert and delete a node while preserving the invariant
Explain how insertion order can degrade a BST to O(n) operations

subtopics.name: Balanced Trees
subtopics.summary: Why balance matters and how rotations restore it.

objectives.text: Explain why balancing guarantees O(log n) operations
Describe how a rotation restores balance after an insertion
Compare a balanced BST with a hash table for ordered access

topics.name: Priority Queues and Heaps
topics.summary: Getting the smallest or largest item efficiently, repeatedly.

subtopics.name: Binary Heaps
subtopics.summary: The heap property, array representation, sift-up and sift-down.

objectives.text: State the heap property and verify it for a given array
Insert into and extract the minimum from a binary heap
Explain the array indexing scheme for parent and child nodes

subtopics.name: Heapsort and Heap Construction
subtopics.summary: Building a heap in linear time and sorting in place.

objectives.text: Describe how heapsort sorts in place using a heap
Explain why bottom-up heap construction is O(n), not O(n log n)
Compare heapsort with merge sort on time and space

subtopics.name: Priority Queue Applications
subtopics.summary: Scheduling, event simulation and greedy algorithms that need the next-best item.

objectives.text: Model a scheduling problem using a priority queue
Explain the role of a priority queue in a greedy algorithm
Choose between a heap and a sorted list for a given usage pattern

topics.name: Graph Algorithms
topics.summary: Traversing networks — the first algorithms that operate on relationships rather than sequences.

subtopics.name: Representing Graphs
subtopics.summary: Adjacency matrices and adjacency lists, and their space and time trade-offs.

objectives.text: Build an adjacency list and an adjacency matrix for a given graph
Compare the space cost of each representation for sparse and dense graphs
State the cost of enumerating a vertex's neighbours in each representation

subtopics.name: Breadth-First and Depth-First Search
subtopics.summary: Two traversal orders, the structures behind them, and what each discovers.

objectives.text: Trace BFS and DFS from a given start vertex
Explain why BFS uses a queue and DFS uses a stack
Use BFS to find the shortest path in an unweighted graph

subtopics.name: Weighted Shortest Paths
subtopics.summary: Dijkstra's algorithm, edge relaxation, and why negative weights break it.

objectives.text: Trace Dijkstra's algorithm on a small weighted graph
Explain the relaxation step and the role of the priority queue
State why Dijkstra's algorithm fails with negative edge weights
